prompt: Five people earn R$ 2,000, R$ 2,200, R$ 2,300, R$ 2,500 and R$ 21,000 a month. What is the mean, in reais?
For the same five salaries, R$ 2,000, R$ 2,200, R$ 2,300, R$ 2,500 and R$ 21,000, what is the median, in reais?
hint: The third of five, once sorted.

prompt: Horta's mean salary is R$ 5,338.89 and its median R$ 2,400. Which sentence describes the staff honestly?
hint: Which summary describes the middle person?

choices.text: The average employee earns about R$ 5,300, so most earn near that
choices.why: Eight of the nine earn less than R$ 3,500; nobody earns near the mean.

choices.text: A typical employee earns about R$ 2,400
choices.why: Right. The median is what the middle person earns; four earn less and four earn more.

choices.text: The salaries cannot be summarised because one is so different
choices.why: They can: the median summarises the typical salary well, and the mean answers the payroll question.

choices.text: The mean is wrong and should be recalculated
choices.why: The mean is arithmetically right; it answers a different question from the one about typical pay.

prompt: Horta's founder doubles their own pay to R$ 56,000. What happens to the median salary?
hint: Does the order of the nine salaries change?

choices.text: It doubles too
choices.why: Only one value changed, and it was not the middle one.

choices.text: It rises by about R$ 3,100, a ninth of the increase
choices.why: That is what happens to the mean: R$ 28,000 more shared over nine people.

choices.text: It moves up one place, to R$ 2,600
choices.why: The order of the nine is unchanged, so the fifth value is the same person's salary.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. The fifth sorted salary is still R$ 2,400; the founder is still above the middle.

prompt: In the 400 baskets, the mean is R$ 82.78 and the median R$ 66.74. What does that tell you about the shape of the data?
hint: Which way do large values pull the mean?

choices.text: A tail of large baskets on the right
choices.why: Right. Large values pull the mean towards them, so a mean above the median signals a right tail.

choices.text: There is a tail of small baskets on the left
choices.why: A left tail would pull the mean below the median; here it is above.

choices.text: The data is symmetric, since both are between R$ 60 and R$ 90
choices.why: A gap of R$ 16 on a median of R$ 67 is large; in symmetric data the two would nearly agree.

choices.text: Half the baskets are above R$ 82.78
choices.why: Half are above the median, R$ 66.74. Only about a third are above the mean.

prompt: 259 of the 400 baskets are below the mean. What percentage is that? Give two decimal places.
Scores on an easy internal test have a mean of 7.1 and a median of 8.3, out of 10. What is the most likely shape?
hint: This time the mean is below the median.

choices.text: A tail of high scores on the right
choices.why: A right tail would put the mean above the median. Here the mean is below it.

choices.text: Two equal groups, one at 7 and one at 8
choices.why: Two equal groups would put the mean and the median close together, between them.

choices.text: Most did well, with a tail of low scores on the left
choices.why: Right. A ceiling at 10 stops the top from stretching, while a few low scores drag the mean down below the median.

choices.text: Symmetric, because the test was easy
choices.why: An easy test bunches scores near the top, which is the opposite of symmetric.

prompt: With order H-1048 typed as R$ 2,126.00 instead of R$ 212.60, by how many reais does the mean of the twelve baskets rise? Give two decimal places.
hint: The total rises by 2126.00 − 212.60; share that over twelve.

prompt: What is the breakdown point of the median?
hint: How many values must go wrong before the middle is a wrong one?

choices.text: One value out of n
choices.why: That is the mean's: one wild value is enough to move it anywhere.

choices.text: A quarter of the data, the share outside the middle half
choices.why: The median survives far more than a quarter: any corruption of fewer than half the values leaves it in place.

choices.text: Half the data: any fewer bad values leave it among the honest ones
choices.why: Right. Until half the values are corrupted, the median stays among the honest ones.

choices.text: It has none, since the median cannot be moved by any change in the data
choices.why: Change enough values — half — and the median can be moved as far as you like.

prompt: Horta's mean basket jumped from R$ 79 to R$ 239 in one report while the median stayed at R$ 68. What should the analyst do first?
hint: Is the extreme value an error or a real order?

choices.text: Find the value that moved the mean and check its source
choices.why: Right. A jump like that comes from one extreme value; whether it is a slipped decimal or a genuine order decides what to do next.

choices.text: Report the median instead, since it is robust
choices.why: Switching summaries hides the question: is the large value an error or a real order? Look first.

choices.text: Delete the largest basket and recompute
choices.why: If the basket is real, deleting it removes real money; if it is a typo, it should be corrected, not deleted.

choices.text: Report both numbers and let readers decide
choices.why: Reporting both is a good habit, but not before knowing whether one of the inputs is simply wrong.

prompt: Trim one value from each end of 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 40. What is the trimmed mean?
A spreadsheet's TRIMMEAN(A2:A401, 0.2) is applied to 400 baskets. How many baskets does it drop in all?
hint: The argument is the total share removed.

choices.text: 160: 80 from each end
choices.why: That would be a 20% cut at each end; the argument is the total share, split between the two.

choices.text: 40, all of them from the top
choices.why: A trimmed mean cuts both ends, not only the large values.

choices.text: 20, 10 from each end
choices.why: 0.2 is a share, 20%, not a count of twenty.

choices.text: 80: the 40 smallest and the 40 largest
choices.why: Right. 20% of 400 is 80 in total, half from each end.

prompt: As the share trimmed from each end grows from 0% towards 50%, the trimmed mean moves from which summary towards which?
hint: What is left when nothing is trimmed? And when almost everything is?

choices.text: From the median towards the mean
choices.why: It is the reverse: trimming nothing is the mean, trimming everything but the middle is the median.

choices.text: From the mean towards the median
choices.why: Right. The mean and the median are the two ends of the trimmed-mean family.

choices.text: From the mode towards the mean
choices.why: The mode plays no part in trimming.

choices.text: From the smallest value towards the largest one in the data
choices.why: Trimming removes values from both ends symmetrically, so it never heads for an extreme.

prompt: Horta must know how much money to have in the bank on payday. Which summary of salaries answers that?
hint: The question ends in a sum.

choices.text: The median, because it ignores the founder
choices.why: The founder still has to be paid. Median × 9 is R$ 21,600, less than half the payroll.

choices.text: The mean, times nine
choices.why: Right. The mean is the total shared out, so mean × 9 is exactly the R$ 48,050 payroll.

choices.text: The 10% trimmed mean, a compromise between the two
choices.why: Trimming drops real salaries from the total, so the payroll would come up short.

choices.text: The mode, the salary most people receive
choices.why: Two people earn R$ 2,100; the mode says nothing about the total.

prompt: Horta expects 520 orders next month and its mean basket is R$ 82.78. What revenue should it plan for, in reais? Give a whole number.
Match each question to the summary that answers it honestly.
hint: Totals, the middle person, protection against one extreme.

pairs.left: What does next month's payroll cost?
What does a typical employee earn?
What would a fair score be if one judge might be biased?

prompt: A company recruiting staff says its 'average salary' is R$ 5,300. Its median is R$ 2,400. What is the best reading of the claim?
hint: Which centre would the company prefer to quote, and why?

choices.text: False, because the real average salary is R$ 2,400
choices.why: R$ 2,400 is the median. 'Average' was not defined, and the mean really is R$ 5,300.

choices.text: Meaningless, since salaries cannot be averaged at all
choices.why: Salaries are on a ratio scale; the mean is allowed and answers the payroll question.

choices.text: Reliable, because a mean uses every salary
choices.why: Using every salary is exactly what lets one large salary carry it far from typical pay.

choices.text: True, but the summary was chosen to look large
choices.why: Right. The mean is correct and includes the founder; the median would have described a typical job.

prompt: Which report of delivery times hides the least?
hint: Name the summary, report both when they differ, give the count.

choices.text: Median 37 minutes, mean 39, over 12 deliveries
choices.why: Right. It names both centres, so the gap hints at slow deliveries, and the count says how much to trust it.

choices.text: Average delivery: 39 minutes
choices.why: It does not say which centre, how many deliveries, or whether there is a tail.

choices.text: Deliveries are fast
choices.why: No number at all; nothing can be checked.

choices.text: Mean delivery 38.958333 minutes
choices.why: Six decimals add false precision and still hide the median, the count and the tail.

prompt: A city's median house price rose 2% in a year while its mean price rose 15%. What most likely happened?
hint: Which summary moves when the top of the market grows?

choices.text: Most houses rose in value by about 15%
choices.why: Then the median, the middle house, would have risen by about that much too.

choices.text: The mean was miscalculated
choices.why: Nothing suggests an error; a few expensive sales can produce exactly this.

choices.text: More very expensive houses were sold
choices.why: Right. A few large values pull the mean up while the middle of the market barely moves.

choices.text: Cheap houses fell in price, pulling the median down
choices.why: The median rose 2%; and cheap houses falling would lower the mean as well, not raise it.
